purpose: Authoritative-vendor evidence delta promoting Acumatica and SYSPRO from discovery-queued to spec-verified on existing reusable API profiles, and cataloguing Octave Tempo Operations Management (formerly Hexagon j5) as a new high-value frontline-operations system without inventing an outward API. No credentials, customer data, writes, private endpoints or plant-network access were used.

patch.evidenceNote: Acumatica 2026 R1 documentation verifies OAuth 2.0/OIDC plus REST, OData and SOAP data access. WFM selects Authorization Code with PKCE and does not use Acumatica's also-documented Implicit or Resource Owner Password Credentials flows because those grants are disabled by the global connector policy. Contract-based REST endpoints are versioned and customer customizations can change the exposed contract. API user, concurrent request and request-per-minute limits are license-dependent, so the connector must discover the customer's effective limits rather than hard-code generic throttles. Reads stay on explicitly allowlisted resources and generic inquiries; mutative HTTP methods remain disabled.

requiredPermissions: tenant-specific registered OAuth application using Authorization Code with PKCE and the minimum api scope required for approved read surfaces
dedicated least-privilege Acumatica user/role limited to the required company, branches, production, inventory and finance records
read-only REST/OData/Generic Inquiry access to approved production, labour, work-centre, inventory and cost objects; no release, posting, schedule mutation or transaction creation authority
only request api:concurrent_access when customer capacity and the integration design actually require it
dataAvailableOrExpected: production orders, routing operations, quantities, status, priority, start/end dates and work-centre schedules where the customer's endpoint exposes them
manufacturing labour transactions/hours, machine/tool/overhead/material cost context and production cost variance
work centres, machine capacity, finite/infinite schedule context and bottleneck/capacity information when APS is licensed
inventory, warehouse/site, lot/serial, shortages, MRP demand and vendor/outside-processing context
branches, companies, cost centres/financial dimensions and GL attribution needed to relate workforce cost to manufacturing outcomes
customer-defined fields and Generic Inquiry projections explicitly published for integration
automationOpportunities: refresh staffing demand from production orders, work-centre schedules, shortages and APS constraints without changing the Acumatica schedule
compare planned versus actual manufacturing labour hours and payroll/time evidence to identify leakage, missed time and labour-cost variance
use order priority, material availability and work-centre capacity to reduce overtime or agency labour on work that cannot yet run
attribute paid labour, overtime and agency cost to production orders, branches, sites and financial dimensions for finance reporting
use MRP/shortage and outside-processing context to improve labour forecasts and avoid staffing against blocked production
after separate write certification only, export approved labour/time results through a narrowly scoped idempotent interface rather than granting generic ERP mutation authority
savingsHypotheses: reduce avoidable overtime and idle labour by aligning labour plans to current production orders, material constraints and work-centre capacity
reduce payroll and job-cost leakage by reconciling WFM payable time with Acumatica manufacturing labour and production-order actuals
reduce manual finance reconciliation by reusing branches, production orders and financial dimensions for labour attribution
shorten implementation mapping by reusing established sites, work centres, employees/resources, inventory and production structures
improve labour forecasting by joining MRP/APS demand, production priority and historical labour performance
dataGaps: Acumatica is not necessarily the authoritative source for absence, contractual availability, legal work eligibility, detailed skills or agency-worker commercial terms
manufacturing modules, APS, quality and Generic Inquiry exposure vary by customer licence and configuration
contract-based REST endpoint versions and customer customizations can change fields and object shape, requiring schema fingerprints and mapping-version control
API capacity is licence-specific; web-service users, concurrent requests and requests per minute must be discovered in the target instance
OAuth's api scope permits API access but does not by itself prove that the backing Acumatica user has least-privilege read-only business permissions
constraintsRisks: Acumatica documents Authorization Code, Implicit and Resource Owner Password Credentials flows; WFM must force Authorization Code/PKCE and keep implicit/password grants disabled
REST/OData/SOAP surfaces can perform writes as well as reads, so route and HTTP-operation allowlists are required even with a restricted user
the API is tenant-aware and the connected application is registered in a tenant; tenant, branch and company identifiers must be pinned and reconciled explicitly
customer customizations and endpoint versions can create schema drift and custom fields that differ between environments
license-level concurrency and request-rate constraints require adaptive throttling, bounded pagination and retry/backoff rather than fixed aggressive polling
partial failures across production, inventory and financial reads must preserve source timestamps and avoid presenting mixed-age snapshots as one consistent planning state
valueReview.nextDevelopmentAction: Keep Acumatica at spec verification. Reuse the existing REST/OpenAPI, OData and SOAP profiles; add an Acumatica-thin mapping preset that discovers endpoint version, company/branch scope, Generic Inquiry/custom fields and licence API limits. In an authorised sandbox or tenant, use Authorization Code with PKCE, prove the effective user role is read-only, sample no more than the approved records, validate pagination/concurrency/backoff and normalise production orders, work-centres, labour actuals, cost dimensions and MRP/APS context before promoting evidence.

patch.evidenceNote: SYSPRO's current documentation verifies an OData 4.0 service that provides RESTful, controlled, read-only data access for third-party applications. It is supported for on-premise and SYSPRO Cloud ERP; cloud customers must use OData because direct database access is unavailable. OData operators use Basic authentication over HTTPS and the service is licensed/capacity constrained. WFM deliberately chooses this read-only OData data plane instead of e.net/business-object write paths. The catalogue fails closed to customer edge because the same product can be on-prem; an authorised cloud deployment may later prove and pin a direct vendor-cloud route without changing protocol semantics.

requiredPermissions: dedicated SYSPRO OData operator restricted to the approved company/system entities and read-only tables or Business Activity Queries
HTTPS with customer-approved certificate validation; no plaintext Basic authentication
Data Connector - OData entitlement or approved ISV runtime-product route where applicable
for on-premise deployments, terminate access through the customer/site edge rather than exposing the ERP service or SQL Server directly
no e.net business-object mutation, SQL write access, production transaction posting or MOM outbound transaction authority
dataAvailableOrExpected: company and system data exposed as OData 4.0 entities, including customer-approved Business Activity Queries
work centres, machines, employees/resources, production orders, operations, materials and scheduling context where the relevant SYSPRO manufacturing/MOM modules expose them
inventory, purchasing, sales demand and supplier context used to explain production constraints
financial/company dimensions needed for labour and production-cost attribution
MOM/APS schedule and production-operation context where installed, while outbound labour/completion/scrap/material transactions remain outside read authority
automationOpportunities: refresh labour demand from production orders, operations, materials and current work-centre/APS schedule without touching production transactions
join WFM time and payroll evidence to SYSPRO order, work-centre and finance context for labour-cost attribution and variance analysis
reduce overtime or agency requests when material, machine or production-order constraints make planned work unavailable
reuse company, site, work-centre, employee/resource and manufacturing structures during implementation to reduce manual configuration
after separate write certification only, consider narrowly scoped labour/completion hand-off through an approved write integration rather than broad e.net authority
savingsHypotheses: reduce unnecessary overtime and agency cover by matching staffing to executable production orders and material/work-centre constraints
reduce labour-to-order and payroll reconciliation effort by reusing controlled OData entities instead of manual exports
reduce implementation effort by reusing established SYSPRO organisation, manufacturing and scheduling structures
improve labour-cost-per-order and labour-efficiency reporting by joining payable time to production and financial dimensions
reduce security/operations cost versus direct database access by using the vendor-supported read-only OData layer
dataGaps: the exact table/entity set depends on the customer company, enabled modules, OData configuration and Business Activity Queries
SYSPRO is not necessarily authoritative for absence, skills/certifications, employment contract details or agency-worker commercials
cloud and on-prem network routes differ even though the OData semantics are shared
licensing and operator/API capacity must be confirmed per customer; public documentation does not establish one universal request-rate number
older MOM deployments may use live SQL inbound integration internally, but WFM must not infer that direct SQL is an approved external integration route
constraintsRisks: Basic authentication is acceptable only over validated HTTPS and only for a dedicated OData operator with demonstrably read-only effective access
on-prem OData can sit inside a protected network; HTTPS alone does not justify direct cloud-to-plant connectivity
SYSPRO Cloud forbids direct database access, so cloud integrations must not fall back to SQL when OData is unavailable
company/system database entities and customer BAQs can expose broad fields; data minimisation and explicit entity/column allowlists are required
multi-company and multi-site identifiers require deterministic reconciliation before labour or finance attribution
pagination/query expansion and concurrency must be bounded to avoid overloading ERP or breaching licensed API capacity
valueReview.nextDevelopmentAction: Keep SYSPRO at spec verification. Reuse the OData adapter as the preferred WFM data plane, with REST transport semantics, and fail closed to customer edge until the target deployment is proven cloud-hosted or an edge route is configured. In an authorised environment, verify the dedicated OData operator's effective table/company scope, TLS chain, licensed capacity and query limits; then read a bounded set of manufacturing/finance entities or approved BAQs, normalise them, and only promote after read round-trip, pagination/retry and multi-company reconciliation evidence.

systems.name: Octave Tempo Operations Management (formerly Hexagon j5)
systems.evidenceNote: Current vendor pages identify Octave Tempo Operations Management as the product formerly known as j5 Operations Management. The platform covers operations management, shift execution, procedures, safety/compliance, maintenance coordination and contextual operational data. Legacy Hexagon j5 product URLs now redirect to the Octave domain. Historical vendor material documents j5 connectors to historians, CMMS/DCS and SAP, but the current public material reviewed in this cycle does not establish a stable outward read API, authentication model, pagination/rate-limit contract or supported direct database schema for a WFM client. WFM therefore catalogues the product and value without inventing a connector. The cross-host product migration is documentation/identity evidence only; it does not permit customer-data requests to follow redirects automatically.

requiredPermissions: an explicitly vendor-supported read-only Tempo/j5 extraction, reporting or integration identity once the current interface contract is obtained
site/area/asset/shift scope limited to the workforce-planning use case
read access to shift handover, logbook, work-instruction, standing-order, operator-round or contextual operational records only where the licensed deployment exposes them
no approval, permit, standing-order acknowledgement, workflow transition, control-system action or maintenance/ERP write authority
no reliance on legacy Hexagon URLs or undocumented database schemas as a customer-data integration path
dataAvailableOrExpected: shift handover records, operating status, unresolved issues and cross-shift context managed by the operations-management product
operations logbook events and manually or automatically captured plant observations
work instructions, standing orders, acknowledgements and task/workflow status where licensed
operator-round observations and measurements where licensed
asset/equipment, CMMS, historian/DCS and other contextual data already brought into the product through supported connectors
audit and approval context around operational procedures and handovers
automationOpportunities: surface unresolved handover issues, abnormal operating conditions and work-instruction workload to labour planners before the next shift
correlate operational/logbook events with staffing level, overtime, skills mix and production outcomes to identify recurring labour or reliability patterns
use operator-round and maintenance context to anticipate extra inspection, maintenance or specialist labour demand
reuse site/asset/area context already maintained in Tempo/j5 to accelerate mapping once a supported read interface is proven
after a separately certified write interface only, consider narrow task/notification hand-offs without granting general workflow or process-control authority
savingsHypotheses: reduce shift-start delay and duplicated administration by bringing unresolved operational handover items into planning context
reduce avoidable overtime by identifying abnormal plant conditions or maintenance workload before labour is committed
reduce downtime response time by joining operations-log and equipment context to available qualified workers
improve supervisor productivity by reducing manual copying between shift handover/logbook systems and workforce planning
improve executive insight by correlating operational reliability and safety context with labour cost and staffing decisions
dataGaps: no current public outward API/authentication contract was verified, so usable WFM extraction remains unproven
legacy product pages now redirect to a new vendor/domain and the exact product/version migration path can vary by customer
customer IndustraForm/forms/workflows and fields are highly configurable and require tenant-specific schema discovery
historian, CMMS, DCS or SAP data visible inside Tempo/j5 may be contextual copies rather than authoritative source records
the product is not normally authoritative for payroll, employment contracts, absence entitlement or agency-worker commercials
constraintsRisks: older j5 connector descriptions prove interoperability but not necessarily an outward supported API for WFM; directionality must be verified
legacy Hexagon j5 URLs redirect across host/domain to Octave; customer-data traffic must remain host-pinned and must not follow that migration implicitly
operations-management workflows can be safety-critical; no task, approval, permit, standing-order or control write may be inferred from read use cases
site forms and workflow schemas can vary heavily, so schema fingerprints and customer-specific mappings are mandatory
plant/process values may already be transformed or copied from historians/DCS and must preserve source lineage and timestamps
on-premise or protected-site deployments may require customer-edge extraction even if the eventual interface uses ordinary HTTPS
valueReview.nextDevelopmentAction: Keep Octave Tempo/j5 at discovery-queued with no adapter. Obtain current Octave product documentation or an authorised customer integration guide that explicitly defines a supported outward read interface, authentication, versioning, pagination/rate limits, deployment topology and object model. Only then select an existing REST/OData/SOAP/file/database/vendor-thin profile, pin the current Octave host and any legacy-version boundary, build fixture mappings for handover/logbook/work-instruction/round records, and advance to spec verification.
